answer: A farm must thus either lie, which the grove graph proves on replay, or recruit 17 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the harbor registry records each claim and the jade audit publishes every slash. Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 42% of the attester's bond. That is 17 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
